# Extraction rules

<!-- generated by formal-sva 1.1.0; regenerate with `fv.py rules --design ...`; do not edit -->
Inputs: `spec/spec.md` and, when present, `schemas/structured_spec.json`.

1. A feature is a named capability from the specification. Keep its class
   (`Mandatory`, `Optional`, ...) exactly as written.
2. A requirement is the smallest statement that can be checked independently.
   Do not split one sentence into several requirements just to increase the
   count, and do not merge independent clauses.
3. `Statement` must be a paraphrase that keeps the normative words (`shall`,
   `must`) and the exact numbers, polarities and signal names.
4. `Evidence` must be a verbatim clause from the specification. It is checked
   after markdown and whitespace normalization.
5. `Source` is a line or range (`L12` or `L12-L18`) in the spec Markdown.
6. `Clarity` is one of `clear`, `ambiguous`, `incomplete`, `conflicting`,
   `missing_info`, `untestable`.
7. A non-clear requirement must carry `Question`, `Owner` and `Blocking`.
   Owners are `spec_agent`, `spec_engineer`, `architecture_engineer`,
   `rtl_agent` or `verification_engineer`.
8. `Proposed property` is one of `always`, `next`, `response`, `stability`,
   `reset_value`, `cover`, `assume`, `static` or `unknown`.
9. If the specification says nothing about a behavior, do not invent it.
   Record a question instead.
10. A requirement about internal state that is not visible at a top-level port
    is `static` or `not_formalizable`; it is still extracted and still visible
    in the coverage report.
11. `formal/spec/requirements.md` records the `spec_sha256` it was extracted
    from. A changed spec stops extraction. Review and update the extraction
    against the new text, then run `fv.py extract --update-spec-hash`; do not
    use `--force`, which discards the reviewed extraction.
